extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and prospective MathOverflow users/participants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and informal standards for asking, answering, commenting, and otherwise participating on MathOverflow — a research-level mathematics Q&A site running on Stack Exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q&A format — ask particular questions with definite answers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Q&A format encourages people to ask particular questions which can be given definite answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MO is not intended to fill the same niche as math blogging; it is much more focused on 'smaller' and 'more technical' questions, especially ones that have definite answers. If you want to discuss something more broadly, use a blog or other forum instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not a discussion site / limited role for discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: MO is not a discussion site: the framework forces any discussion to remain fairly focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some discussion will take place in comments (requests for clarification, pointing out errors), but extended or broad discussion (e.g., polymath-style collaborative problem-solving) is discouraged on MO and better suited to blogs or other venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments: purpose and length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are intended primarily for clarification or pointing out errors; comments are limited to 600 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the Q&A format and comment length limit, use comments only for focused points (clarification, corrections) rather than extended discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question suitability / topical focus
rubrics_metrics.description: MO will be much more focused on 'smaller' and 'more technical' questions, especially ones that have definite answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current activity is concentrated in areas like algebraic geometry, TQFTs and homological algebra (reflecting the user base). Users are encouraged to ask and answer to broaden coverage of their fields; inappropriate or off-topic questions have been handled by the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting surfacing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and answers get voted up and down, making it easy to find the gems in a large pool of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers change order as later ones get voted up; use votes to identify high-quality content. Active voting is a primary mechanism for quality control and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation system and privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a reputation system: as your questions and answers get voted up, your reputation increases and grants site privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The more reputation you get, the more the system allows you to do. Above 10,000 reputation, there is little difference between users and moderators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you reach 2000 reputation, you can edit other people's posts to correct typos and make the presentation clearer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits are intended to improve clarity and presentation. Use editing privileges responsibly to fix mistakes and improve readability rather than to change substantive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Wiki behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and answers can be marked 'community wiki', in which case all established users (100+ reputation) can edit them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community wiki posts are collaborative by design; marking a post community wiki signals that broader editing and communal ownership is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: When you post material on the site, it is under the Creative Commons Attribution Share-alike license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should be aware their posted material will be shared under CC BY-SA terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math formatting / LaTeX support (temporary guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is currently no LaTeX support (at time of writing); LaTeX support is a top-priority feature to be added later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the meantime, type raw LaTeX, use basic HTML entities (e.g. Ω and x<sub>1</sub>), or write math as you would in email. Expect LaTeX rendering to be implemented once the software exits beta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of account/OpenID issues (procedural guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Google-issued OpenID changes and the site does not recognize you, create a new user and email the site admin; accounts can be merged and alternate OpenIDs added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If persistent problems occur, use a non-Google OpenID (e.g., myopenid.com). (This is operational guidance rather than an evaluative criterion for content.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Community moderation of inappropriate questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The community monitors and deals with inappropriate questions; early experience showed only a few inappropriate questions which were handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before worrying about low-quality influx (e.g., calculus homework), browse existing questions to see how such cases are addressed. For now this has not been a major problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta discussion locus
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta discussion and broader comments/criticisms about MO are being centralized in the blog comment thread (as of this post).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated meta venue for complaints about bugs, community behavior, moderator actions, or site design (including non-technical feedback like color scheme).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to participate to shape coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Users are encouraged to ask and answer questions and invite colleagues to influence the development and encourage good coverage of their field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active participation is the recommended way to broaden topical coverage and improve the site's usefulness for particular subfields.
